key_insight: Adding the ADR physical PV efficiency model to TSMixer offers limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting compared with a purely data-driven baseline.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, physics integration may add complexity without reliably improving accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical model with TSMixer through feature augmentation.
Build a second hybrid architecture using residual learning.
Compare hybrids with the data-driven baseline across training convergence, accuracy, geographic transfer, and limited-data performance.
evidence_signal: Evaluation used over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries, finding slightly faster apparent convergence but no consistent gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
watch_item: These findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or solar-cell design tasks.
paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
